answer: Use per-epoch credential nullifiers. Each identity proves in zero knowledge that it holds one scarce outside credential, say one per verified operator, and publishes hash(credential, epoch). A second key on the same credential repeats that nullifier and is refused, so a whole plume of clones lands on one ledge. A 50-sybil farm needs 50 real credentials, so cost grows 1:1 with N while the proof stays crystal clear and private. Failure mode: rented credentials; random 10-minute re-proofs catch them.
